title: Sellaronda Week: Alta Badia & Val Gardena on One Pass
subRegion: Alta Badia & Val Gardena, Dolomites, South Tyrol

bestPeriod.window: Mid-January-mid-March; late February and early March give the longest lift days with the Sellaronda still comfortably completable
bestPeriod.avoid: 27 December-6 January (Italian holiday peak, Sellaronda bottlenecks at Passo Pordoi) and after mid-April, when the low Corvara and Ortisei returns close
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-January-mid-March; late February and early March give the longest lift days with the Sellaronda still comfortably completable

food.note: Rifugio pasta €14, €20, secondi €22, €30; one gourmet dinner adds €120, €250

transport.note: Airport transfer €70, €120 each way; SkiBus free with the guest card; two ski-taxi legs

summary: This is the week the Dolomites were built for: one keycard, twelve ski areas, and a ring road on snow around a 3,152 m limestone block. The structure is simple, bed down in Alta Badia, spend the first days learning the local network at Corvara, La Villa and San Cassiano, run the **Sellaronda** once in each direction mid-week, take a day off the circuit for the **Hidden Valley** behind Lagazuoi, and cross into **Val Gardena** for the Saslong and Seceda. The skiing is overwhelmingly blue and red, immaculately groomed and rarely steep; what makes it remarkable is the scale, the light on the Sella and Sassolungo, and a rifugio culture in which lunch is a two-hour Ladin meal rather than a tray of chips. It suits confident intermediates above all, families who want distance without difficulty, and experts who accept that their hard skiing here is two World Cup pistes and a handful of couloirs rather than a whole mountain.

itinerary.title: Arrive Corvara, orient on Col Alt and Piz La Ila
itinerary.morning: Transfer from Venice or Verona up the Val Badia. The road from Brunico climbs through San Lorenzo and San Martino; from the south you come over the Passo Falzarego, which is the more dramatic and the more likely to be chained.
itinerary.afternoon: Collect skis at Sport Kostner in Corvara and buy the 6-day Dolomiti Superski pass online the night before to take the 5% discount. Ride Col Alt for the easy reds above the village, then cross to **Piz La Ila** for a first look at the Gran Risa from the side.
itinerary.evening: La Stüa de Michil at Hotel La Perla in Corvara if you want the Michelin start to the week; otherwise Ristorante Stüa dla Lâ, or a plate of casunziei in the hotel.
itinerary.dayStats: Transfer 2 h 45-3 h 30 / Corvara 1,568 m / 12-15 piste km, roughly 2,000 m descent / pass 5% cheaper bought online

itinerary.title: Alta Badia network and the Gran Risa
itinerary.morning: Work the local 130 km: Corvara to Colfosco, back over to La Villa via Piz La Ila, then down into San Cassiano and up Piz Sorega. This is intermediate cruising at its most efficient, long, wide, empty reds.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the **Gran Risa** at La Villa, the World Cup giant-slalom hill: short at about 1.25 km but with pitches past 50%, and best attempted at 14:00 once you have found your edges. Then a long lunch at Ütia de Bioch or Rifugio Piz Arlara.
itinerary.evening: Après at the Piz Arlara terrace or the Corvara base bars, then dinner at La Siriola in Ciasa Salares, San Cassiano, if you booked it.
itinerary.dayStats: 30-35 piste km / roughly 5,500 m descent / Gran Risa 1.25 km, ~450 m vertical, max gradient past 50% / free Alta Badia SkiBus with the guest card

itinerary.title: Sellaronda clockwise (orange)
itinerary.morning: Leave Corvara by **08:45**. Up over **Passo Campolongo (1,875 m)** to Arabba, then the Porta Vescovo cable car and across to **Passo Pordoi (2,239 m)**. Arabba is the steepest section of the whole circuit and the only place the orange route bites.
itinerary.afternoon: Over **Passo Sella (2,244 m)** into Val Gardena, up Plan de Gralba and **Dantercepies**, then over **Passo Gardena (2,121 m)** to Colfosco and home. Lunch fast and standing if you left late, the circuit does not forgive a two-hour rifugio.
itinerary.evening: Corvara, feet up. You have done roughly 26 km on skis and a dozen lifts.
itinerary.dayStats: Sellaronda orange ~40 km total, ~26 km skied / four passes 1,875-2,244 m / 6 h including lifts / start by 10:00, last pass by 15:30

itinerary.title: The Hidden Valley and Lagazuoi
itinerary.morning: Ski via San Cassiano and Capanna Alpina, or take the ski taxi, to **Passo Falzarego**, then the **Lagazuoi cable car** to 2,732 m. Have a coffee on the Rifugio Lagazuoi terrace first, it is the best single view in the Dolomites.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the **Armentarola** red, 8.5 km down the Val Travenanzes between frozen waterfalls, stopping at **Rifugio Scotoni** for the grill. At the bottom, join the **horse-drawn rope tow**, €5, cash, which drags a line of skiers back toward the Armentarola lift.
itinerary.evening: San Cassiano for dinner; take the free SkiBus home to Corvara rather than the last lift chain.
itinerary.dayStats: Lagazuoi cable car every ~15 min, 09:00-16:40, 3 min ride, top 2,732 m / Armentarola run 8.5 km red / horse tow €5 pp / Capanna Alpina→Piz Sorega taxi ~€5 pp; Armentarola→Falzarego ~€8 pp cash

itinerary.title: Weather-contingency and rest day: Ortisei, Ladin culture, tobogganing
itinerary.morning: This is the flex day, take it here, or move it to whichever day the Sella passes close on wind, which they do several times a season. Ride the **Ortisei-Alpe di Siusi** cable car onto the plateau and ski two or three gentle blues in the sun, or skip skis entirely.
itinerary.afternoon: Ortisei's woodcarving workshops and the Museum Gherdëina, or the **Museum Ladin Ćiastel de Tor** at San Martino in Badia, the Ladin language survives in about 30,000 speakers across these five valleys and this is where it is explained properly. Then the **Rasciesa toboggan run**, roughly 6 km from the funicular back to Ortisei.
itinerary.evening: Anna Stuben or Concordia in Ortisei; take the free Val Gardena SkiBus and the Alta Badia connection home, or stay over.
itinerary.dayStats: Alpe di Siusi plateau ~1,800-2,000 m / Rasciesa toboggan ~6 km / zero World Cup pistes, deliberately / SkiBus free with guest card

itinerary.title: Val Gardena, Seceda and the Saslong
itinerary.morning: Ride into Val Gardena over Passo Gardena, then take the **Seceda** gondola from Ortisei to **2,518 m** for the Odle ridge view and the long descent back toward Santa Cristina.
itinerary.afternoon: Up **Ciampinoi** from Selva and ski the **Saslong**, the FIS World Cup downhill piste, including the Gobbe di Cammello camel humps that eat racers every December. Lunch at **Rifugio Emilio Comici**, which serves seafood and champagne at 2,150 m and is exactly as absurd as it sounds.
itinerary.evening: Selva for après at the Ciampinoi base, then the last lifts over Passo Gardena, **do not be later than 16:00** on this crossing.
itinerary.dayStats: Seceda 2,518 m / Saslong FIS downhill, roughly 3.4 km, start ~2,250 m to ~1,420 m / Val Gardena-Alpe di Siusi 175 km on 79 lifts / Passo Gardena return hard cutoff ~16:00

itinerary.title: Sellaronda counter-clockwise (green), then out
itinerary.morning: Run the circuit the other way if you have a late flight: **green, counter-clockwise**, out over Passo Gardena to Selva and Plan de Gralba first, then Sella, Pordoi, Arabba and Campolongo home. It skis completely differently, flatter early, steeper late.
itinerary.afternoon: If your flight is early, do half the loop to Arabba and take the SkiBus back. Return hire kit by 17:00; most shops shut at 18:30.
itinerary.evening: Overnight near Venice or Verona rather than driving the Falzarego in the dark after snowfall.
itinerary.dayStats: Sellaronda green ~40 km / half-loop escape via Arabba + SkiBus ~45 min / transfer to VCE 2 h 45-3 h 15 / winter tyres or chains mandatory 15 Nov-15 Apr

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Col Alto
accommodationStrategy.description: Sits at the foot of the Col Alt lift in the centre of Corvara, which is the single best Sellaronda start point because you can leave clockwise or counter-clockwise from the same door. Ski depot, spa, and half board that gets you fed before an 08:45 departure. Roughly €150, €250 pppn half board.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Portillo Dolomites 1966
accommodationStrategy.description: On the pass itself between Corvara and Arabba, so you start the circuit already 300 m higher and ahead of the village queues, and the Arabba side is a ski-out. The trade is isolation: no village to walk to in the evening. Roughly €130, €200 pppn.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Gran Baita
accommodationStrategy.description: The Val Gardena alternative if the Saslong and Seceda matter more to you than Alta Badia. Walking distance to the Ciampinoi and Dantercepies stations, so both Sellaronda directions and the World Cup piste are on the doorstep. Roughly €140, €230 pppn half board.

logistics.connectivity: 4G and 5G are good in both valleys and on most of the Sellaronda, weak in the Val Travenanzes on the Hidden Valley. EU roaming applies. Download the Dolomiti Superski and Alta Badia apps for live lift status, the Sella passes close on wind without much warning.
logistics.emergency: 112. Piste rescue is charged in Italy and the bill for a sled-and-ambulance can run into hundreds of euros; helicopter recovery is far more. Italy is EU, so EHIC/GHIC covers state healthcare, but not rescue costs, insurance naming winter sports is essential and many Italian resorts now require third-party liability cover by law.
logistics.weather: The dominant pattern is high pressure and cold, dry air, with occasional Adriatic lows delivering heavy snow to the south side. The real disruptor is **wind on the four passes**, which shuts the exposed Pordoi and Sella lifts and breaks the circuit mid-day. A **temperature inversion** is common: Corvara at −12°C and Piz La Ila at −2°C.
logistics.bookingWindows: Half-board hotels for February half-term and Christmas go 6-9 months out. Michelin tables at La Siriola and La Stüa de Michil need 3-6 weeks. Rifugio Scotoni and Club Moritzino take lunch bookings and fill by 11:00 on a bluebird day. Ski school for a peak week: 2-3 months.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted essentially everywhere including rifugi, but the **Lagazuoi horse tow and the Armentarola ski taxis are cash**, carry €30, €40 in small notes. Tipping is rounding up; a coperto of €2, €4 per head is normal and is not a tip.
logistics.transportRules: **Winter tyres or onboard chains are legally required in South Tyrol and Veneto from 15 November to 15 April**, and the Falzarego and Pordoi roads are enforced. Passes load onto the reloadable MyDolomiti Card, €5 to replace. Free SkiBus travel comes with the local guest card issued by your hotel, ask for it at check-in, it is not automatic.
logistics.permits: The Dolomites are a UNESCO World Heritage site; drones are effectively banned over the ski areas and need ENAC compliance elsewhere. Italian law requires **helmets for under-18s** and mandates **third-party liability insurance for all skiers**, most lift passes now bundle it, but confirm.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable. Altitude tops out around 2,700 m and is not a medical issue. The Sella couloirs (**Val Mezdì, Val Setus, Val Lasties**) are unpatrolled ski routes with terrain traps and no phone signal, take a guide, transceiver, shovel and probe, and read **lawinen.report** every morning.

proTips: Do the Sellaronda on a Tuesday or Wednesday. Weekends bring Italian day-trippers up from Bolzano and Belluno and the Pordoi bottleneck can add 40 minutes to the loop.
Leave Corvara by 08:45, not 09:30. The circuit is timed by the last pass crossing at 15:30, and every ten minutes you lose in the morning is ten minutes off your lunch.
Buy the pass online the night before for the 5% discount, and put it on a MyDolomiti Card you keep between trips, it reloads and saves the queue entirely.
Book Rifugio Scotoni by phone before you ride the Lagazuoi cable car. It is the best lunch on the mountain and by the time you ski down to it the terrace is gone.
Ride Lagazuoi at 09:00 sharp. The Hidden Valley is a one-way run served by a single cable car; by 11:30 you are skiing in a queue and by 15:00 the horse tow has a twenty-minute line.
Ski the Gran Risa in the afternoon and the Saslong in the morning. The Gran Risa is south-facing and needs sun on it; the Saslong is best on hard overnight groom before it gets chopped.
Ask for the local guest card at hotel check-in. It makes the Alta Badia and Val Gardena SkiBus free, which is what rescues you when a pass closes on wind.
Carry €40 in cash purely for the horse tow and the two Armentarola ski taxis. Card readers do not exist on any of them.
If the Sella passes shut, do not sit in the hotel, take the SkiBus to Ortisei and ski the sheltered Alpe di Siusi plateau, which stays open in almost anything.

raw.Pass tiers by name: Three products. The **local Val Gardena-Alpe di Siusi pass** covers 79 lifts and 175 km, **€72, €80 adult per day**, **€50, €56 junior under 16**, **€65, €72 senior over 65**. The **Alta Badia local pass** covers roughly 130 km on 53 lifts at similar money. The area/regional super-pass is **Dolomiti Superski**: 12 areas, about **1,200 km** and 450 lifts on one card, at **€77, €86 adult per day**, **€54, €60 junior**, **€69, €77 senior**. A **6-day Dolomiti Superski adult pass falls in the region of €420, €480** in high season with juniors around 30% less, banded, not confirmed, because Dolomiti Superski now prices through a calculator rather than a fixed tariff. There is a **5% discount for buying online**, and the **Superdays** bundle gives 10 non-consecutive days at **€660 adult / €460 junior**. Passes load onto the **MyDolomiti Card**, a reloadable keycard: rather than a deposit you pay a **€5 replacement charge** if you lose it. Season 2025/26 ran **29 November 2025 to 3 May 2026**. There is no meaningful night skiing here, the after-dark product is floodlit tobogganing, not floodlit pistes.
raw.The Sellaronda, both directions: The circuit rings the Sella massif over four passes: **Campolongo (1,875 m), Pordoi (2,239 m), Sella (2,244 m) and Gardena (2,121 m)**, through Selva, Canazei, Arabba, Corvara and Colfosco. Total **roughly 40 km, of which about 26 km is on skis** and the rest on lifts, across a dozen installations. **Orange is clockwise**, from Val Gardena via the **Dantercepies** gondola out of Selva; **green is counter-clockwise**, entering through Plan de Gralba. Allow **six hours including lifts and lunch**. The governing rule is timing: **start by 10:00 at the latest, and cross your last pass by 15:30.** Miss that and you are in a taxi.
raw.Named lifts that structure the week: **Ciampinoi** and **Dantercepies** out of Selva; **Piz Sella** and Plan de Gralba on the Sella side; **Seceda** gondola from Ortisei to 2,518 m; the Ortisei-Alpe di Siusi cable car; **Piz La Ila** and Piz Sorega from La Villa and San Cassiano; **Boè** from Corvara up toward the Vallon and the highest lift-served point in Alta Badia; Col Alt above Corvara. The bus links that patch gaps are the free **SkiBus** networks in both valleys, the Alta Badia line between Corvara, Colfosco, La Villa, San Cassiano and Badia, and the Val Gardena line between Ortisei, Santa Cristina and Selva.
raw.Snow reliability: Bases sit at **1,236 m (Ortisei), 1,433 m (La Villa), 1,563 m (Selva) and 1,568 m (Corvara)**, tops at **2,518 m (Seceda)** and around 2,550 m at Vallon. That is not a high resort by Alpine standards, and the Dolomites' answer is engineering: Dolomiti Superski publishes snowmaking coverage of **roughly 97% of pisted kilometres**, one of the highest figures in the Alps, drawing on reservoirs across all twelve areas. It is also a dry, cold, high-pressure climate, natural snowfall is modest but what falls stays. **In a bad snow year the Dolomites out-perform almost everywhere else**, because the machine-made base is laid in late November and holds; what suffers is the off-piste, which is often simply absent, and the low returns into Ortisei and Corvara, which close first.
raw.Off-piste and touring: This is not a freeride destination, and the honest lines are few. The **Vallon bowl** above Corvara holds the best lift-accessed powder in Alta Badia. **Val Mezdì**, the great couloir splitting the Sella massif from the Pordoi cable car, and its neighbours **Val Setus** and **Val Lasties**, are the classic Dolomite descents, steep, committing, terrain-trapped and **effectively guide-only**: they are ski routes, not pistes, unpatrolled, and people die in them most seasons. The avalanche bulletin is the **Euregio bulletin at lawinen.report** covering Tyrol, South Tyrol and Trentino, with **AINEVA** the national umbrella. Guides: the **Guide Alpine Alta Badia** and **Catores** in Val Gardena.
raw.Piste breakdown: Dolomiti Superski's 1,200 km runs approximately 30% easy, 60% intermediate and 10% difficult, an unusually intermediate-heavy mountain. **Beginners** belong on the Alpe di Siusi plateau above Ortisei, which is a vast, gentle, sunny shelf, and on the Piz Sorega side of San Cassiano. **Intermediates** own everything, and should simply ski the Sellaronda twice and the Alta Badia network in between. **Experts** get the **Saslong** in Val Gardena, the FIS downhill dropping from Ciampinoi to Santa Cristina with its Gobbe di Cammello camel humps; the **Gran Risa** at La Villa, a short, brutal giant-slalom pitch of roughly 1.25 km and 450 m vertical with gradients past 50%; and the Sella couloirs with a guide.
raw.The Hidden Valley: The single best non-circuit day. Ride the **Lagazuoi cable car** from Passo Falzarego to **2,732 m**, which runs about every 15 minutes from 09:00 to 16:40 on a three-minute lift, then ski the **8.5 km Armentarola red** down the Val Travenanzes past frozen waterfalls. At the bottom you are pulled back toward the Alta Badia lifts by a **horse-drawn rope tow, €5 per person**, two horses and a long rope, genuinely the last of its kind. A shuttle taxi from Capanna Alpina to the Piz Sorega base is about **€5 per person**; Armentarola back to Passo Falzarego runs about **€8 per person, cash only**.
raw.Non-ski days and rifugio culture: Lunch is the point: **Rifugio Scotoni** on the Hidden Valley for grilled meat, **Club Moritzino** on Piz La Ila, **Ütia de Bioch** and **Rifugio Piz Arlara** in Alta Badia, **Rifugio Emilio Comici** above Selva for its improbable seafood and champagne list, **Baita Sofie** on Seceda. Off snow: the **Rasciesa toboggan run** above Ortisei, roughly 6 km; night tobogganing from Piz Sorega; the **Museum Ladin Ćiastel de Tor** at San Martino in Badia for the Ladin language and culture; woodcarving workshops and the Museum Gherdëina in Ortisei; the Pranives ice rink in Selva.
raw.Hire, lockers and schools: **Sport Kostner** in Corvara and the **Rent and Go** and Skiservice outlets across Selva, La Villa and Ortisei cover hire at roughly **€110, €180 a week** standard and **€200, €280** performance; boot-and-ski depots at most lift bases run **€6, €10 a day** and save you carrying kit through villages. Schools: **Scuola Sci & Snowboard Alta Badia** (Corvara), **Ski School Dolomites La Villa**, **Scuola Sci Selva Val Gardena** and **Scuola Sci Ortisei**. Expect roughly **€250, €350 for five half-day group mornings** and **€65, €90 an hour** for a private, with the hourly rate dropping on full-day and multi-day bookings.

sources.confidenceNotes: **The 6-day Dolomiti Superski adult price of €420, €480 is an inferred band, not a confirmed figure**, Dolomiti Superski publishes only a dynamic calculator, and this must be re-checked against live dates before publishing. The Alta Badia local pass price is likewise unconfirmed. The **97% snowmaking coverage figure is resort-published marketing** and should be attributed or softened. Saslong and Gran Risa length and vertical figures are from general reference rather than an FIS homologation sheet, spot-check. Alta Badia's 130 km / 53 lifts and the 30/60/10 difficulty split are indicative. Hotel rates, ski school and hire prices are prior-season bands. Michelin star counts for La Siriola and La Stüa de Michil change annually and must be re-verified against the current guide. Rifugio opening and booking practice varies year to year. The Italian third-party liability insurance requirement and helmet law should be confirmed against current statute before publishing as legal advice.
